moTa: Bản rút gọn kiểu IELTS Academic: Listening 20 câu (đăng ký lớp gốm · giới thiệu thư viện) + Reading 20 câu (vì sao ta ngáp · xe đạp công cộng).

nhom.huongDan: Part 1 — Câu 1–10. Nghe cuộc gọi đăng ký lớp học buổi tối và điền vào phiếu. Mỗi chỗ trống viết MỘT TỪ hoặc MỘT SỐ. Chỉ nghe MỘT lần.

nghe.t: Good morning, Riverside Community Centre. Diane speaking. How can I help you?
Oh, hello. I picked up one of your leaflets last week, and I'm interested in the pottery course for beginners. Are there any places left?
Let me have a look. Yes, you're in luck, we've still got a few. I'll just need to take some details. Could I have your surname, please?
Yes, it's Haldane. That's H, A, L, D, A, N, E.
Thank you. And your first name?
Marcus.
Lovely. And what's your address, Marcus?
It's 14 Orchard Road. Orchard, like the place where apple trees grow.
Got it. Now, the beginners' class runs twice a week, on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Which would you prefer?
Tuesday would suit me better, actually.
Oh, I'm sorry, I've just seen that the Tuesday group is already full. There's only space on Thursday.
That's all right. I'll take Thursday, then. How long does the course last?
It used to be ten weeks, but this term we've made it shorter, so it's eight weeks now. Each class is two hours, from seven to nine.
Fine. And is it a big group? I'd like to get some help from the teacher.
Don't worry. A few years ago we took fifteen people, but now the maximum is twelve, so everyone gets plenty of attention.
Great. How much does it cost?
The full price is one hundred and twenty pounds. But you live locally, so you pay the reduced fee, which is ninety-five pounds.
That's good news. Does that cover everything?
It covers all the clay you use, and the tools as well. The only extra is if you want your pots sent to your home, and most people just carry them.
And do I need to bring anything?
You don't need an apron, we lend you one. But it does get messy, so bring an old shirt to wear on top of your clothes.
Good idea. Is there anywhere to park? I'll be driving straight from work.
The car park in front of the centre is for staff only, I'm afraid. Students can park behind the library, which is just next door. It's free after six.
Perfect. And when does the course actually start?
We were planning to begin on the second of October, but the teacher is away that week. So the first class is on the ninth of October.
The ninth of October. I'll put it in my diary. Can I pay now, over the phone?
Of course. Let me just get the payment screen up.

cau.de:
EVENING CLASS REGISTRATION — Pottery for beginners
Surname: ___
cau.giaiThich: Người gọi đánh vần: 'It's Haldane. That's H, A, L, D, A, N, E.' Với tên riêng được đánh vần, hãy viết từng chữ cái ngay khi nghe; dễ nhầm A với E.

cau.de: Address: 14 ___ Road
cau.giaiThich: 'It's 14 Orchard Road. Orchard, like the place where apple trees grow.' orchard = vườn cây ăn quả; người nói giải thích nghĩa để bạn viết đúng chính tả.

cau.de: Class day: ___
cau.giaiThich: Bẫy: anh ấy muốn Tuesday nhưng 'the Tuesday group is already full. There's only space on Thursday' rồi anh đồng ý 'I'll take Thursday'. Đáp án là thông tin cuối cùng được chốt.

cau.de: Length of course: ___ weeks
cau.giaiThich: 'It used to be ten weeks, but this term … it's eight weeks now.' used to = trước đây (nay không còn) nên ten là bẫy; two hours và seven to nine là giờ học, không phải số tuần.

cau.de: Maximum class size: ___ people
cau.giaiThich: 'A few years ago we took fifteen people, but now the maximum is twelve.' fifteen là con số của quá khứ; maximum = tối đa.

cau.de: Fee for local residents: £ ___
cau.giaiThich: 'The full price is one hundred and twenty pounds. But you live locally, so you pay the reduced fee, which is ninety-five pounds.' 120 là giá đầy đủ (bẫy); reduced fee = phí đã giảm.

cau.de: Fee includes: clay and ___
cau.giaiThich: 'It covers all the clay you use, and the tools as well.' cover = include (bao gồm) là cặp paraphrase; việc gửi sản phẩm về nhà mới phải trả thêm.

cau.de: Bring: an old ___
cau.giaiThich: 'You don't need an apron, we lend you one. But … bring an old shirt.' apron (tạp dề) là bẫy vì trung tâm cho mượn; thứ phải tự mang là áo sơ mi cũ.

cau.de: Parking: behind the ___
cau.giaiThich: 'The car park in front of the centre is for staff only … Students can park behind the library.' Bãi trước trung tâm chỉ dành cho nhân viên; behind = phía sau.

cau.de: First class: ___ October
cau.giaiThich: 'We were planning to begin on the second of October, but the teacher is away that week. So the first class is on the ninth of October.' Ngày 2 là kế hoạch cũ đã bị đổi.

nhom.huongDan: Part 2 — Câu 11–20. Nghe thủ thư giới thiệu thư viện cho sinh viên mới và chọn A, B hoặc C. Chỉ nghe MỘT lần.

nghe.t: Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the Hartley Library. My name's Priya and I'm one of the librarians here. I know you've had a long day of talks, so I'll keep this short, and then you're free to explore the building.

Let's begin with opening hours. During term time, the library is open from eight in the morning until ten at night on weekdays. At weekends we close earlier, at six. Some of you may have heard that we're open twenty-four hours. That's only true in the exam period in May, so please don't turn up at midnight in October.

To get in, you'll need your student card. You should have collected it this morning. If you forget it, the staff at the front desk can let you in, but only once each term. After that you'll have to go home and get it, so keep it in your wallet.

Now, borrowing. First-year students can take out up to ten books at a time. Most books can be kept for three weeks. However, books that are in high demand, the ones with a red sticker, are one-week loans. If you return a book late, we no longer charge money. Instead, you won't be able to borrow anything else until it comes back. In my experience, that works much better than a fine.

The building has four floors. The ground floor, where we are now, has the café and the group study area, so talking is fine here. The first floor is for quiet study, which means you can whisper but not hold a conversation. The top two floors are silent. Phones must be switched off there, not just turned down.

Many of you will want to work together on projects. We have eight group rooms, and you must book them in advance. You can't do this at the desk. You have to use the library app, and you can book up to two hours a day.

Printing is something students often ask about. The printers are on the first floor, next to the stairs. You pay with your student card, so put some money on it online first. The machines don't accept coins.

If you need help finding material for an essay, don't just type words into a search engine. Each subject has its own librarian. Mine is history, for example. You can make an appointment with your subject librarian by email, and a meeting usually lasts about thirty minutes.
Finally, a word about food. Cold drinks with a lid are allowed everywhere. Hot drinks and snacks must stay in the café. We made this rule last year, after someone spilled soup on a very old map.

Before you leave, there's one thing I'd like you all to do. Don't worry about joining a tour today, there'll be tours all next week. Just go to the front desk and pick up the printed guide, because it has the floor plan and all the passwords you'll need. Thank you, and enjoy your time here.

cau.de: On weekdays during term time, the library closes at
luaChon: six in the evening.
ten at night.
no time, as it stays open all night.
cau.giaiThich: 'open from eight in the morning until ten at night on weekdays.' Sáu giờ là giờ đóng cửa cuối tuần; mở 24 giờ chỉ đúng vào mùa thi tháng Năm — hai bẫy distractor điển hình.

cau.de: A student who forgets their student card
luaChon: can be let in by staff one time per term.
has to pay for a replacement card.
will not be allowed in under any circumstances.
cau.giaiThich: 'the staff at the front desk can let you in, but only once each term.' once each term = one time per term (paraphrase). Không hề nhắc tới việc trả tiền làm thẻ mới.

cau.de: Books with a red sticker can be borrowed for
luaChon: three weeks.
ten days.
one week.
cau.giaiThich: 'books that are in high demand, the ones with a red sticker, are one-week loans.' Three weeks là hạn của sách thường; ten là số sách được mượn, không phải số ngày.

cau.de: What happens if a student returns a book late?
luaChon: They must pay a small fine.
They cannot borrow more books until it is returned.
Their student card stops working for a week.
cau.giaiThich: 'we no longer charge money. Instead, you won't be able to borrow anything else until it comes back.' no longer = không còn nữa nên phương án phạt tiền (fine) sai.

cau.de: On the first floor, students
luaChon: may speak very quietly to each other.
can hold group discussions.
must switch their phones off.
cau.giaiThich: 'The first floor is for quiet study, which means you can whisper but not hold a conversation.' whisper = speak very quietly. Thảo luận nhóm là ở tầng trệt, tắt điện thoại là ở hai tầng trên cùng.

cau.de: How do students book a group study room?
luaChon: by asking at the front desk
by sending an email
by using the library app
cau.giaiThich: 'You can't do this at the desk. You have to use the library app.' Email được nhắc sau đó nhưng là để hẹn thủ thư chuyên ngành, không phải đặt phòng.

cau.de: Before using the printers, students need to
luaChon: add money to their student card.
bring some coins with them.
ask a member of staff for help.
cau.giaiThich: 'You pay with your student card, so put some money on it online first. The machines don't accept coins.' put money on = add money to. Máy không nhận tiền xu nên B sai.

cau.de: What does the speaker say about subject librarians?
luaChon: They will correct drafts of students' essays.
They are at the front desk every day.
Students need to arrange a time to see them.
cau.giaiThich: 'You can make an appointment with your subject librarian by email.' make an appointment = arrange a time. Họ giúp TÌM tài liệu cho bài luận chứ không sửa bài.

cau.de: Which of these may students take to the silent floors?
luaChon: a cup of hot coffee
a bottle of water with a lid
a sandwich
cau.giaiThich: 'Cold drinks with a lid are allowed everywhere. Hot drinks and snacks must stay in the café.' Chai nước có nắp là đồ uống lạnh có nắp; cà phê nóng và bánh mì phải để ở quán.

cau.de: What does the speaker ask the students to do before they leave?
luaChon: join a tour of the building
download the library app
collect a printed guide
cau.giaiThich: 'Don't worry about joining a tour today … Just go to the front desk and pick up the printed guide.' pick up = collect. Tour bị gạt đi ngay ('Don't worry about…'), app không được nhắc ở đoạn này.

nhom.huongDan: Passage 1 — Câu 21–30. Câu 21–24: True / False / Not Given. Câu 25–27: chọn A–D. Câu 28–30: điền MỘT TỪ lấy nguyên văn từ bài đọc.
nhom.doan:
WHY DO WE YAWN?

A  Everybody yawns. We do it when we wake up, when we are bored in a meeting and, strangely, when we simply read about yawning. Babies yawn before they are born, and so do most animals with a backbone, from fish to birds. Yet although the action is so common, scientists still do not fully agree on what it is for.

B  For many years, the most popular explanation was that a yawn brings extra oxygen into the blood. According to this idea, we yawn when the air in our lungs becomes 'stale'. The theory sounds sensible, but it was tested in the 1980s and failed. Volunteers who breathed air with extra oxygen yawned just as often as those who breathed normal air. Exercise, which makes the body demand far more oxygen, did not make people yawn more either.

C  A more recent suggestion is that yawning cools the brain. Like a computer, the brain works best within a narrow range of temperatures, and it heats up when we are tired or have been concentrating for a long time. A deep yawn pulls cool air into the mouth and increases the flow of blood to the skull, which may carry heat away. Supporters of this theory point out that people yawn less when they hold something cold against the forehead. In one study in a hot desert city, people walking outdoors also yawned less often in summer, when the air was as warm as their bodies, than in the cooler winter months.

D  Whatever its physical purpose, yawning is also social. Seeing, hearing or even thinking about a yawn can set off another one, and this 'contagious' yawning is not present from birth. Children usually begin to catch yawns at around four or five years of age, the same period in which they become better at understanding other people's feelings. Research also suggests that we are more likely to catch a yawn from a relative or a close friend than from a stranger. For this reason, some psychologists believe that contagious yawning is linked to empathy. Others are less sure, and argue that the results of such studies have been difficult to repeat.

E  Contagious yawning is not limited to humans. Chimpanzees catch yawns from members of their own group, and dogs have been observed yawning after their owners do. One possible advantage is that a shared yawn helps a group to stay alert at the same moment, which would be useful if danger were near. For now, however, this remains an attractive idea rather than a proven fact. The humble yawn, it seems, still keeps some of its secrets.

cau.de: Human babies start to yawn before birth.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn A: 'Babies yawn before they are born.' before they are born = before birth ⇒ True.

cau.de: Experiments in the 1980s supported the oxygen theory.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B: 'it was tested in the 1980s and failed.' Thí nghiệm bác bỏ chứ không ủng hộ (supported) giả thuyết ⇒ False.

cau.de: Yawning lowers the temperature of the brain more effectively than placing something cold on the forehead.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C chỉ nói người ta ngáp ÍT hơn khi áp vật lạnh lên trán, không hề so sánh cách nào làm mát não hiệu quả hơn ⇒ Not Given. Bẫy: có đủ từ khoá nhưng không có phép so sánh.

cau.de: Contagious yawning can be observed in newborn babies.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn D: 'this contagious yawning is not present from birth' và trẻ thường bắt đầu lúc 4–5 tuổi ⇒ trẻ sơ sinh chưa ngáp lây ⇒ False. Đừng nhầm với câu 21 (ngáp thường).

cau.de: What did the experiments described in paragraph B show?
luaChon: Extra oxygen made no difference to how often people yawned.
People yawn more after they have taken exercise.
Stale air in the lungs is the main cause of yawning.
Yawning reduces the amount of oxygen in the blood.
cau.giaiThich: 'Volunteers who breathed air with extra oxygen yawned just as often as those who breathed normal air.' just as often = no difference. B ngược bài ('did not make people yawn more'); C là chính giả thuyết đã bị bác.

cau.de: According to paragraph C, a yawn may cool the brain by
luaChon: lowering the temperature of the air in the lungs.
giving the brain a short rest from concentrating.
bringing in cool air and sending more blood to the skull.
making a tired person feel more awake.
cau.giaiThich: 'A deep yawn pulls cool air into the mouth and increases the flow of blood to the skull, which may carry heat away.' pulls in = brings in; increases the flow = sends more. Các phương án khác không có trong bài.

cau.de: Why do some psychologists connect contagious yawning with empathy?
luaChon: It has been found in every study that has been carried out.
Babies are able to do it before they are born.
People catch yawns most easily from strangers.
It develops at the age when children begin to understand others' feelings.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn D: trẻ bắt đầu ngáp lây lúc 4–5 tuổi, 'the same period in which they become better at understanding other people's feelings'. C ngược bài (dễ lây từ người thân hơn người lạ); A sai vì kết quả 'difficult to repeat'.

cau.de: The writer compares the brain to a ___, which also works best within a limited range of temperatures.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C: 'Like a computer, the brain works best within a narrow range of temperatures.' Like … = compares … to; narrow range = limited range.

cau.de: People are less likely to catch a yawn from a ___ than from someone they know well.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn D: 'we are more likely to catch a yawn from a relative or a close friend than from a stranger.' Câu hỏi đảo chiều so sánh (more likely ⇄ less likely); someone they know well = relative / close friend.

cau.de: Yawning together might allow the members of a group to remain ___ at the same time.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn E: 'a shared yawn helps a group to stay alert at the same moment.' stay = remain; at the same moment = at the same time. alert = tỉnh táo, cảnh giác.

nhom.huongDan: Passage 2 — Câu 31–40. Câu 31–34: True / False / Not Given. Câu 35–37: chọn A–D. Câu 38–40: điền MỘT TỪ lấy nguyên văn từ bài đọc.
nhom.doan:
FOUR GENERATIONS OF SHARED BICYCLES

A  In 1965, a group of activists in Amsterdam painted about fifty bicycles white and left them on the streets for anyone to use, free of charge. The plan was simple and generous, and it failed almost at once. Within a month, most of the bikes had been stolen or thrown into the canals, and the police removed the rest. Even so, the idea of a public bicycle refused to disappear.

B  Thirty years later, Copenhagen tried again with a more careful design. Its bikes were heavy, brightly coloured and built from unusual parts that would not fit ordinary bicycles, which made them less attractive to thieves. Riders unlocked one by putting a coin into a slot, and got the coin back when they returned the bike to a rack. The system was popular, but because users remained anonymous, bikes were still lost in large numbers.

C  The real change came with technology. From the late 1990s, schemes in French cities began to ask riders to register with a card, so that every journey could be connected to a named person. When Paris opened its own scheme in 2007, with thousands of bikes available at stations a few hundred metres apart, cycling in the city rose sharply and other capitals hurried to copy it. In these 'third-generation' systems, the first half hour is often free. This encourages short trips and keeps bikes moving between stations rather than sitting outside one office all day.

D  Around 2016, a fourth generation appeared: bikes without stations. Each bicycle carried its own lock and could be found and opened with a smartphone, then left wherever the journey ended. Companies, most of them in China, placed millions of these bikes in cities in a very short time. Riders loved the freedom, but pavements were soon blocked, and photographs of huge piles of unwanted bikes went around the world. Several companies collapsed, and many cities introduced rules about how many bikes could be put on the streets and where they could be parked.

E  Today, shared bikes are a normal part of urban transport, and electric models have made them practical in hilly cities and for older riders. Studies of their effects, however, give a mixed picture. Many journeys on shared bikes replace walking or public transport, not car trips, so the reduction in traffic is smaller than supporters once hoped. On the other hand, people who try a shared bike are more likely to buy a bicycle of their own later. Perhaps the greatest benefit, then, is not the journeys themselves but the habit they create.

cau.de: The white bicycle scheme in Amsterdam operated successfully for several years.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn A: 'it failed almost at once. Within a month, most of the bikes had been stolen…' Thất bại gần như ngay lập tức, trái với 'successfully for several years' ⇒ False.

cau.de: Copenhagen's bikes were made with parts that could not be used on normal bicycles.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B: 'built from unusual parts that would not fit ordinary bicycles'. would not fit = could not be used on; ordinary = normal ⇒ True.

cau.de: Riders in Copenhagen had to return a bike to the rack they had taken it from.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B chỉ nói trả xe 'to a rack' (một giá bất kỳ) thì lấy lại xu, không nói có bắt buộc đúng giá ban đầu hay không ⇒ Not Given.

cau.de: The number of people cycling in Paris increased after its scheme opened.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C: 'When Paris opened its own scheme in 2007 … cycling in the city rose sharply.' rose sharply = increased ⇒ True.

cau.de: Why were so many bikes lost in Copenhagen?
luaChon: The bikes looked too similar to ordinary ones.
Nobody knew who had taken them.
The racks were too far apart.
Riders did not get their coin back.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B: 'because users remained anonymous, bikes were still lost in large numbers.' anonymous = không ai biết danh tính. A ngược bài (xe trông khác hẳn), D ngược bài (trả xe thì lấy lại xu).

cau.de: What is the purpose of making the first half hour free?
luaChon: to attract tourists who are visiting the city
to compete with bikes that have no stations
to persuade riders to register with a card
to keep bikes in circulation through short journeys
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C: 'This encourages short trips and keeps bikes moving between stations rather than sitting outside one office all day.' keeps bikes moving = keep in circulation. Du khách và xe không trạm không được nêu là lý do.

cau.de: What problem did the station-free bikes cause?
luaChon: They were left in places where they got in people's way.
Riders had to walk a long way to find one.
Their locks were easily broken by thieves.
There were too few of them to meet demand.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn D: 'pavements were soon blocked, and photographs of huge piles of unwanted bikes went around the world.' Vỉa hè bị chặn = xe cản lối đi. D ngược bài: xe quá NHIỀU ('millions', 'unwanted').

cau.de: In Copenhagen, a bike was unlocked when the rider inserted a ___.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B: 'Riders unlocked one by putting a coin into a slot.' putting … into = inserted. Không điền slot vì slot là khe nhận xu, không phải thứ được bỏ vào.

cau.de: Fourth-generation bikes could be located and unlocked using a ___.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn D: 'could be found and opened with a smartphone'. found = located; opened = unlocked. Không điền lock: khoá gắn trên xe, còn công cụ để mở là điện thoại.

cau.de: The writer suggests that the main advantage of shared bikes may be the ___ that they encourage.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn E: 'Perhaps the greatest benefit, then, is not the journeys themselves but the habit they create.' greatest benefit = main advantage; create = encourage. Bẫy: journeys bị phủ định bằng 'not … but …'.
